_note: Run from the repository root: node bin/mutation-proof.mjs --spec fixtures/example-project/mutations.json — the exit code is 1 because two of these are UNCLEAR on purpose.

mutations.name: the id guard in placeOrder
mutations._expect: FIRED — 'rejects an order without an id' and 'rejects an empty id' both go red.

mutations.name: the zero-width stripper
mutations._expect: FIRED — 'strips a zero-width space' goes red.

mutations.name: the zero-width test datum
mutations._expect: FIRED — and read WHICH tests go red. 'detects a zero-width space' and 'hasInvisible is not stateful across calls' fail; 'strips a zero-width space' stays GREEN, because with an empty constant its assertion reads "ab" === "ab". Red is not proof until you have checked which assertion tripped. This mutation is the evidence behind the entry in control-chars.baseline.json.

mutations.name: the id written into the created event
mutations._expect: UNCLEAR — and THIS is the interesting one. A test named 'every order event carries an id' exists and stays green, because its filter matches nothing. The suite claims to guard this. It does not. dead-filters finds the same defect statically.

mutations.name: a mutation whose anchor no longer exists
mutations._expect: UNCLEAR (anchor missing) — a mutation that cannot be applied is never a silent skip. Reported as 'no guard', it would send you off to build one that already exists.
